quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: You are merging onto an interstate highway. You should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: Look for a gap in traffic that is large enough for you to safely enter. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: You should use your horn when:

options.text: Another vehicle is in your way.
It may help prevent a collision.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Use your horn only when it is necessary to avoid a collision. Do not use it to tell a driver or bicyclist to drive faster or get out of your way.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. You must:

options.text: Leave a note on the vehicle.
Report the collision right away to the city police or, in unincorporated areas, to the California Highway Patrol.

questions.explanation: Leave a note with your name, phone number, and address on the vehicle you hit. Also report the collision to your local city police or, if in an unincorporated area, to the California Highway Patrol (CHP).

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Cars on the right go first.
Let crossing traffic pass before you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let crossing traffic pass before you go.
questions.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way at this sign. Slow down and let vehicles and pedestrians cross before you proceed. Stop if necessary.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: To know where traffic is behind you:

options.text: Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror frequently to know where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a two-way street with no curb, your front wheels should be:
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill with no curb, turn your wheels away from the street. If your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: To avoid losing traction on wet roads, you should:
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on wet roads to prevent hydroplaning. Keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, remove your foot from the gas, do not brake, keep the car straight, and let it slow down.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you that you are leaving a one-way highway and entering a two-way highway.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle:

options.text: Expect the child to have full control of the bicycle.

questions.explanation: Children on bicycles are unpredictable. They may suddenly change direction without warning. Children and bicycles are small and easy to miss.

questions.question: Traffic control devices in construction and maintenance work areas are:
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers are used in work zones. Be extra careful when you see them on the road.

questions.question: Which statement is true about roadwork zones?

options.text: Fines are the same in work zones as in normal driving conditions.
You must "Slow for the Cone Zone."
Slow down only if you see workers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must "Slow for the Cone Zone."
questions.explanation: Slow down in work zones to protect drivers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and road workers.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. The pedestrian is in the middle of the street when your light turns green. You should:

options.text: Go if you have the right-of-way.
Go if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait for the pedestrian to finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrian to finish crossing.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you must yield to any vehicle, bicyclist, or pedestrian in the intersection. Wait until the pedestrian has fully crossed before proceeding.

questions.question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm, you should:

options.text: Go at 15 mph if no children are present.
Go at normal speed but watch for children.

questions.explanation: Come to a complete stop and stay stopped until the signal arm is pulled back and the bus moves. This applies whether you are going the same direction as the bus or coming from the opposite side.

questions.question: If weather or light conditions require you to turn on your lights:
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect back and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at collisions or unusual events:
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at collisions or other unusual events. This practice, called "rubbernecking," creates traffic congestion.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Get ready to merge with traffic coming into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to merge with traffic coming into your lane.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that traffic will merge from the right into your lane. You should be ready to let them in safely.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of on the road. What should you do to prevent it in rainy weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.

questions.explanation: Slow down in rainy weather to reduce hydroplaning risk. Driving too fast causes tires to ride up on the water and lose contact with the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When the driver you passed signals you to return to your lane.
When you signal for three seconds.
When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane, make sure you are far enough ahead of the vehicle you passed. Look in your rearview mirror. When you see both headlights of the other vehicle, you have enough room to return to your lane.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.explanation: Never change lanes while inside an intersection. Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Watch for other drivers moving into the same lane as you.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC) and its effects on the body.
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body and reduce its effects.

questions.question: What happens if you misuse a disabled placard?

options.text: Your placard is taken away only.
Your placard is taken away, and you pay a fine and/or go to jail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your placard is taken away, and you pay a fine and/or go to jail.
questions.explanation: Misusing a disabled placard is a crime. You can lose your placard, pay a fine up to $1,000, and spend up to six months in jail.

questions.question: When should you not enter an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red?

options.text: Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection if you cannot clear it before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Touch one rear wheel to the curb.
Use your parking brake and put the car in "park."
Point your front wheels straight if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and put the car in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and leave your car in gear or "park" on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your front wheels away from the center of the road. If there is a curb, turn your wheels toward it when facing downhill, or away from it when facing uphill.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane is ending ahead. Drivers in that lane will need to merge into another lane.

questions.question: When a bicyclist is turning left, what can they do?

options.text: Wait on the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. Expect to see bicyclists in the left lane when they are turning left.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?

options.text: Only when pulling up to the curb.
Both when pulling up to and leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both when pulling up to and leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal when pulling up to a curb and when leaving a curb.

questions.question: You want to pass a bicyclist in a narrow lane when a car is coming toward you. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and pass the bicyclist.
Slow down and let the other car pass before you pass the bicyclist.
Wait for the bicyclist to leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the other car pass before you pass the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Handle one problem at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the bicyclist when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: On a freeway, why should you look farther ahead than on a city street?

options.text: Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle.

questions.explanation: On freeways, watch for changes in traffic ahead. Look for signals from other drivers. Be ready for vehicles merging at ramps and for sudden changes in road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Also adjust your seat, fasten your belt, and secure items in your car before moving. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: At what speed can hydroplaning start?
questions.explanation: Most tires can move water away from the tire at speeds up to 35 mph. Above 35 mph, tires cannot move water as well. Tires may then ride on top of the water like water skis and lose contact with the road.

questions.question: On the freeway, traffic is merging into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for them if you can.
Speed up to keep your spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for them if you can.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, make room for merging traffic.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you, even if they do not help you see much farther.
